chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qassani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about breastfeeding (radāʿ), so he said: 'The free woman is not compelled to breastfeed the child, but the mother of the child (umm al-walad) is compelled.'

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: An enslaved woman who bears her master's child.
key_terms.الرِّضَاعِ: Breastfeeding (radāʿ), the act of nursing which can establish kinship ties.
key_terms.الْحُرَّةُ: A free woman (as opposed to an enslaved woman).

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in breastfeeding obligations between a free woman and an enslaved woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the juristic distinction in compulsory breastfeeding (*radāʿ*) based on social status, reflecting the classical Shia view that an enslaved mother (*umm al-walad*) is legally bound to nurse her child while a free woman is not. This ruling underscores the interplay between personal liberty and familial obligation in Shia fiqh, particularly regarding the establishment of kinship ties and maintenance rights.
